title.narrative: Flood Emergency Reconstruction and Resilience Project

description.narrative: The project will contribute to the economic and social recovery of flood-affected areas in Punjab Province and the northern districts of Haveli, Kotli and Poonch (also known as "northern districts") through the rehabilitation and reconstruction of high-priority infrastructure damaged and weakened during the floods in September 2014. The project focuses on the transitional phase of the emergency response for the rehabilitation and reconstruction of priority roads, bridges, irrigation and flood protection infrastructure damaged by the floods. Providing financing for the most urgently needed works, the loan and grant will enable the Government to redirect its own financing to housing and livelihood cash grants for the most vulnerable groups, thus restoring the economic activity essential to their survival. The project will also support ex ante disaster risk management (DRM) capacity building to mainstream resilience in development planning. Reconstruction of damaged and at-risk infrastructure in the flood-affected areas will use appropriate and cost-effective multi-hazard resistant design and construction standards to mitigate the potential impact of future disasters. The Project's design is based on the findings of the damage assessment reports prepared by the respective Punjab Planning and Development Departments (P&D) in January 2015 and facilitated by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and World Bank, in close coordination with the federal government and other donors.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Flood-damaged roads and bridges in Punjab Province and the districts of Haveli, Kotli, and Poonch reconstructed Indicator: By 2018, 173 km of roads and bridges include safety measures that are friendly to women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. Progress/Status: Overachieved.
At completion, a total of 261.6 km of roads and bridges (206.6 km in Punjab and 55 km in HKP districts) were reconstructed with the targeted safety measures. Data Source: Progress reports and Gender Action Plan Actual value:

Output: 1. Flood-damaged roads and bridges in Punjab Province and the districts of Haveli, Kotli, and Poonch reconstructed Indicator: By the end of 2018, 1,740 km of damaged provincial highways and district roads repaired, rehabilitated, and reconstructed Progress/Status: Overachieved.
A total of 2,598.6 km of provincial highways and districts roads (2,300 km in Punjab and 298.6 km in HKP districts) were repaired, rehabilitated and reconstructed. Data Source: Progress reports provided by the implementing agencies and the Planning and Development Departments Actual value:

Output: 2. Flood-resilient irrigation and flood management infrastructure in Punjab Province implemented Indicator: At least 90% of selected flood protection and irrigation structures damaged by 2014 floods reconstructed and made more resilient by 2018 Progress/Status: Overachieved.
100% of the selected flood protection and irrigation structures were restored and made more resilient under the Project, by using sheet piling at critical reaches. Also, two new flood protection bunds for protection of Jhelum city were constructed.
In total 388 kilometer of flood protection bunds were rehabilitated and 6 km of new flood bonds were /constructed.
Data Source: Punjab Planning and Development Department and PID progress reports. Actual value:

Output: 3. DRM strengthened Indicator: 200 hectares of active slide area along major road corridors treated through bio-engineering interventions by 2018 Achievement: 800 Progress/Status: Overachieved.
At completion, at total of 1,158.6 ha of active and potential landslide areas was stabilized in districts of HKP. This includes 193 active roadside landslides spread over an area of 375 ha, and another 783.6 ha area of potential landslides and critical slopes. The focus of the landslide treatment / slope stabilization remained along the roads rehabilitated, repaired and reconstructed under the Project.
The treatment / stabilization work included use of engineering as well as bio-engineering measures such as; construction of retaining walls, breast walls, surface drains to divert water from upstream of the landslide, and plantation of fast growing species. Data Source: Project progress reports.

Output: 3. DRM strengthened Indicator: Gender-disaggregated data and analysis of multihazard vulnerability and risk assessments available for 20 most vulnerable districts by 2018 Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Achieved.
At completion, the MHVRA studies were conducted for 20 project districts with gender-disaggregated demographic data of 1.8 million households living in the project area. The data were collected on: (i) members of the household, (ii) education, (iii) persons with disabilities, (iv) swimming skills, (v) trainings received on disaster management, first aid, civil defense or rescue and (vi) number of men, women and transgender-headed households.
Statistical analysis was conducted on above mentioned parameters. In addition, to bridge gender specific gaps in the primary data, secondary data was also collected and analyzed. A seperate chapter on ‘Gender-based Exposure Vulnerability Assessment' was included in the MHVRA reports. IN addition, the MHVRA atlases prepared for the 20 districts include gender specific maps.
Data Source: Gender Action Plan.

Output: 3. DRM strengthened Indicator: Land-slide risk mitigation measures include procurement of 30% of the forest nurseries owned by women Achievement: 60 Progress/Status: Overachieved.
Plants/seedlings were procured from 24 community and private nurseries, out of these (15) 63% were owned by women against the 30% target. . Plants were procured with a total cost of PKR 2.519 million. Of which plants for PKR 1.76 million (70%) were procured from women owned nurseries. These women earned PKR 23.275 million.
Landslide treatment component also provided an unintended benefit of providing employment opportunities to women where, out of a total 107 forest wardens recruited for watch and ward of the plantation, 29 or 31% were women. Data Source: Project progress reports.

Output: 3. DRM strengthened Indicator: Enhanced safety procedures for dams and flood protection structures institutionalized in PID by 2018 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved.
DRM Consultants have developed SOPs and inspection manuals for dams safety which have been adopted by PID. Data Source: PID Reports. Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
Restoration and reconstruction of critical public and social infrastructure to multihazard resilience standards

By the end of 2018, production of major crops in Punjab equals or is more than pre-flood levels (baseline: 2013/14, in ‘000 tons: Wheat: 18,000 Sugarcane: 43,000 Cotton: 8,900 Progress/Status: Almost achieved except for the cotton.
At completion, the production of major crops in ‘000' tons is as under:
Wheat: 18,377 Sugarcane: 44,906 Cotton: 6,826 *
* The reduction in production of cotton is due to multiple reasons including: (i) spread of red fly diseases, (ii) shifting of cotton production to sugarcane and orchards by the farmers because of lower demand of cotton, as a result of closure of major textile industry owing to shortage of natural gas and very high rise in electricity costs. Data Source: Federal and provincial government statistics on agriculture and cultivated land
Punjab Agriculture Department reports Base year: 2015 Baseline value: N

By the end of 2018, traffic volume of all type of vehicles in 23 flood-affected districts is equal or more than pre-flood levels (baseline 3013/14) Progress/Status: To be assessed during Project completion review. Data Source: Progress reports of Communication and Works Department and subproject completion reports. Base year: 2015 Baseline value: N
